newsitem.title: USA: Mallinckrodt to sell Sensor Systems unit.
newsitem.headline: Mallinckrodt to sell Sensor Systems unit.

text.p: Mallinckrodt Group Inc. said Monday it signed a definitive agreement to sell its Sensor Systems unit to Lexington, Mass.-based Instrumentation Laboratory, a manufacturer of in vitro diagnostic products.
Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
Mallinckrodt Sensor Systems had sales of under $30 million for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1996.
"Mallinckrodt Sensor Systems is a good business but one that no longer fits with our strategic direction," Mallinckrodt Chairman C. Ray Holman said in a statement.
The unit manufacturers point-of-care blood gas and electrolyte in vitro diagnostic products.
The St. Louis-based chemical company, which has sales of $2.2 billion, said on Aug. 29 that it plans to focus more on its core businesses in human healthcare and speciality chemicals.

Mallinckrodt said then that it and its partner, chemicals company Hercules, were seeking to sell their Tastemaker food and beverage flavors joint venture. Mallinckrodt also said it hopes to sell its animal health division, Mallinckrodt Veterinary, which had sales of $456 million last fiscal year.
Mallinckrodt's stock was up 12.5 cents at $41 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
